title: Advanced Air Hockey 3D with Scoring
prompt:
Create a complete HTML file with an advanced 3D air hockey game using Three.js. Follow these specifications precisely:

## Scene Setup
- Use a perspective camera at position (0, 12, 10) looking down at the table at angle.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.5) and a point light above the table at (0, 8, 0) with intensity 1.2.
- Load the 'Lantern.glb' model using GLTFLoader from a CDN. Scale it to 0.5 and place two lantern instances at positions (-4, 0, 0) and (4, 0, 0) on each side of the table as decorative goal markers. Store references in window.__3D_STATE__.lanternLeft and window.__3D_STATE__.lanternRight.
- The table is a flat green box (12 wide x 0.3 tall x 8 deep) centered at origin with a darker border/rim (0.3 units high around edges).
- Add a center line (thin white plane at z=0 spanning the width).
- The puck is a red cylinder (radius 0.3, height 0.15) starting at (0, 0.3, 0).
- Player paddle (blue cylinder, radius 0.5, height 0.2) starts at (0, 0.3, 3). AI paddle (orange cylinder, radius 0.5, height 0.2) starts at (0, 0.3, -3).
- Goals are open areas at z = +4 and z = -4, spanning x from -1.5 to 1.5.

## Physics
- The puck moves with velocity (vx, vz). Apply friction factor 0.998 per frame to simulate air resistance.
- Puck bounces off left/right walls (x = ±6) and top/bottom walls (z = ±4) EXCEPT in the goal areas (|x| < 1.5 at z boundaries).
- Paddle-puck collision: when distance between paddle center and puck center < 0.8, reflect puck velocity away from paddle and add 20% of paddle's movement velocity for realistic transfer.
- Puck speed is capped at 0.3 units per frame.
- All positions must remain NaN-free.

## User Interactions
- Player moves their paddle using mouse movement on the canvas. Raycasting from mouse onto the table plane (y=0.3) determines paddle position.
- Player paddle is constrained to z > 0 (their half) and within table bounds (|x| < 5.5).
- Press 'R' key to reset the game (scores to 0, puck to center, paddles to starting positions).
- A 'Start Game' button in the DOM starts/restarts the puck with a random initial velocity.
- A 'Pause' button toggles game pause state.

## AI Opponent
- The AI paddle follows the puck's x position with a smoothing factor of 0.04 and is constrained to z < 0 (AI half).
- AI paddle z-position oscillates slightly toward the puck's z when puck is in AI half.

## Scoring
- When puck passes z > 4 within goal area: AI scores a point.
- When puck passes z < -4 within goal area: Player scores a point.
- After a goal, puck resets to center with a brief 1-second delay, then launches toward the scorer.
- First to 7 points wins. Show a 'Game Over' message and stop play.

## HUD / UI
- Display scores in a DOM overlay: 'Player: X' on bottom, 'AI: Y' on top, styled with large white text and text-shadow.
- Show a 'Start Game' button (id='startBtn') centered before game begins.
- Show a 'Pause' button (id='pauseBtn') in top-right corner.
- When game ends, show a div (id='gameOverMsg') with winner text.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields:
- playerScore: number (initially 0)
- aiScore: number (initially 0)
- puckPosition: {x, y, z}
- puckVelocity: {x, z}
- playerPaddlePosition: {x, y, z}
- aiPaddlePosition: {x, y, z}
- gameStarted: boolean (false initially)
- gamePaused: boolean (false initially)
- gameOver: boolean (false initially)
- winner: null | 'player' | 'ai'
- lanternLeftLoaded: boolean
- lanternRightLoaded: boolean
- puckSpeed: number (magnitude of velocity)
- lastGoalScorer: null | 'player' | 'ai'

Update __3D_STATE__ every frame from actual Three.js object positions and game logic variables.
physics_constraints: Puck velocity decays by friction 0.998/frame. Puck bounces off walls with reflection. Paddle-puck collision transfers momentum. Speed capped at 0.3. Puck and paddles constrained to table bounds. Positions must be NaN-free at all times.
